question: Where do so many stories of Renaissance genius, like Giotto drawing a perfect circle freehand, come from?
answer: Mostly from one book: Giorgio Vasari's Lives of the Artists, 1550. Vasari, a Medici court painter writing up to two centuries after some of his subjects, set out to crown Florence and his hero Michelangelo. He rarely checked an anecdote. Giotto's perfect O is a Florentine's story about Florence's first great painter.
move: Ask who told the story first and what they gained by telling it.
ask: When I hear a great success story, do I know who first told it, and why?
reference: Giorgio Vasari, The Lives of the Artists, trans. Julia Conaway Bondanella & Peter Bondanella, Oxford World's Classics, 1991
